result.title: Every Premier League team's favourite nationality of player to sign
result.text:
Crystal Palace

Total signings = 79

Number of different nationalities of players signed = 23

Patrick Vieira's youthful revamp has seen the average age of the club's signings fall by over three years, which marks a shift in the club's transfer policy.

But his decision to sign more English players than players from any other nation is in line with Palace's transfer activity in the past decade.

Of the 79 additions, 29 have been English players, with Vieira responsible for five of those transactions. Palace's next favourite nationality of player to sign is French, with 10 players with French heritage joining in the past 10 years.

The signings were made from just 23 countries, seven less than the league average, and Vieira's transactions have remained consistent with that trend, too, with the Frenchman only adding two different nationalities by signing Denmark's Joachim Andersen and US international Chris Richards.

Everton

Total signings = 82

Number of different nationalities of players signed = 33

Everton are another team who tend to choose English players, with their 23 English players accounting for 28 per cent of all of their signings.

Outside of England, Everton have signed more French players than any other nation, having signed seven in the past decade.

Frank Lampard has also signed more English players than any other nation, having signed five English players since he joined in January 2022, with Dele Alli and James Tarkowski among those arrivals, while Neil Maupay's move from Brighton added one more to the list of French players they've signed.

Everton have signed players from smaller nations in the past with mixed results. Their total of 33 nations is three above the league average and includes recruits from Curacao (Cuco Martina), Mali (Abdoulaye Doucoure), Ukraine (Vitaliy Mykolenko) and Venezuela (Salomon Rondon).

Fulham

Total signings = 127

Number of different nationalities of players signed = 41

Fulham have made the second most signings and have used the third highest number of different nationalities in the past decade.

They've also signed 30 players from England, which is roughly one in every three signings they make.

France and the Netherlands are tied in second place when it comes to the club's favourite nationalities to use, having signed seven players from each of those nations — including Frenchmen Issa Diop and Layvin Kurzawa this summer.

With players from 41 different nationalities, Marco Silva's team trail only Brighton and Nottingham Forest in this category. They've also signed players from countries rarely recruited from in the last decade. Manor Solomon represents the third Israeli player to join a Premier League side. Fernando Amorebieta is one of two Venezuelan players to arrive in England's top division in the last decade, along with Salomon Rondon.

Leeds United

Total signings = 110

Number of different nationalities of players signed = 35

Jesse Marsch has only overseen one transfer window at Leeds and the early signs from his transfer activity mark a departure from the types of transactions Leeds carried out in the past decade.

Thirty-four of their 110 signings have been English players, which is the fourth highest total of any team, but Marsch has only signed one Englishman — Darko Gyabi, who joined from Manchester City. Marsch has signed two players from Spain, which is the club's second most-favoured nationality — the arrivals of Marc Roca and Joel Robles takes the number of Spanish players signed by Leeds in the past decade to 10.

The club has signed 35 different nationalities since 2013-14, five higher than the league average, and they haven't been shy in buying players from smaller nations.

One of those is Dexter Blackstock, the only player to represent Antigua & Barbuda and play in the Premier League in the past decade. They also signed Souleymane Doukara a season after they signed Blackstock in 2013-14, one of two players to represent Mauritania and be signed by a Premier League club — the other is former Fulham forward Aboubakar Kamara.

Leicester City

Total signings = 62

Number of different nationalities of players signed = 25

Around one in every four players signed by Leicester in the last 10 years were English.

Nigeria, Spain and Belgium share second place — they have signed four players of each of those nationalities since 2013-14, with Wilfred Ndidi, Youri Tielemans and Ayoze Perez among them.

Leicester have only signed players from 25 countries, which is the sixth-lowest number of any Premier League side, and don't typically take risks on those from nations outside the 10 most popular ones for transfers. They did sign three players from Algeria, though, with Islam Slimani (2016) and Rachid Ghezzal (2018) following in the footsteps of title-season hero Riyad Mahrez, who joined the club during the 2013-14 season.

Patson Daka's arrival last year made him just the second Zambian currently in the Premier League, along with Brighton's Enock Mwepu.

Liverpool

Total signings = 54

Number of different nationalities of players signed = 27
